💬 Iran to pursue war-related environmental damage in international forums: VP

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Vice President and Head of the Department of Environment Shina Ansari has called for documenting and pursuing legal action in international forums over environmental damage caused by recent wars.

During a meeting with the President of the Iranian Red Crescent Society (IRCS), Pir-Hossein Kolivand, and a number of its officials and staff, Ansari praised Red Crescent relief workers for their dedication during the recent war, highlighting their role in strengthening national resilience and alleviating people’s suffering.
​
She described the bombing of fuel storage facilities in Tehran and Karaj, along with other war-related environmental damage, as acts of ecocide and crimes against the environment.
​
Ansari said the damage violated international environmental conventions and its effects remained visible along the country’s southern coasts, coastal wetlands, and ecosystems, warning that the consequences could become more severe in the long term.
​
She added that documentation of the environmental damage caused by the 12-day war had been completed, while documentation of the Ramadan war was ongoing. She said the cases would be pursued in international forums in cooperation with the Presidential Legal Department.
